source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence campus is Kentucky's largest published data center at 5 MW of IT capacity, more than half the state's disclosed 9.55 MW.

The 5 MW is spread across 143,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that capacity is roughly 125 racks. Kentucky has three data centers publishing power figures and five mapped facilities in total, so most of the mapped base discloses nothing and the installed capacity is likely larger than the 9.55 MW on record. By published capacity, the state is not a center of AI scaling activity.

The certifications describe the tenant mix. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and Green Globes qualify the campus for financial, healthcare, federal and audited workloads. Those are compliance-driven enterprise tenants rather than GPU training clusters. The suitability score of 50, a weighted mean of published IT capacity and operator type, reflects that reading, and it is missing announced expansion.

What the data does not cover is the part that decides AI relevance. There is no figure for actual power draw, utility interconnection, available grid capacity, or any expansion plan. A 5 MW enterprise facility becomes an AI facility only if its operator retrofits for higher density and the local grid can supply the load. Neither condition is visible in published specifications.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
